then: That makes sense. Sometimes people put this off for years, but something eventually makes them realize it is time to get it handled. I just want to understand what made this important for you now.
variants: What changed recently that made this feel more important now?
When you say you've been meaning to do this for years, what kept you from moving forward before?
Was there something that happened recently that made you start thinking about this again?
If you waited this long already, what would happen if you put it off again?
Who would be most affected if this still wasn't handled?

instructions.text: Common answers: health concerns, loss of a friend or family member, financial worries, family responsibilities.

nodes.title: Only wants cremation coverage
cue_phrases: I just want enough for cremation

say.text: That makes sense. What made you decide that cremation is the only thing you want covered?
then: That makes sense. A lot of people call in thinking only about the cremation itself, but sometimes there are other small expenses left behind. I just want to make sure we are looking at what your family may actually need, not more than necessary.
variants: When you say you only want enough for cremation, are you mainly trying to keep the cost low, or are you trying to make sure your family doesn't have to worry about anything?
Besides the cremation itself, what other expenses do you think your family might have to handle?
If the cremation was covered but there were still other expenses, who would most likely be responsible for those?
Would it make sense to look at an amount that covers the cremation first, then see if there is room to protect them from a little more?

instructions.text: Many callers underestimate the total cost their family may face.

nodes.title: Says their family will handle it
cue_phrases: My kids will take care of it

say.text: It's wonderful that you have children willing to step up. If you had the choice, would you rather leave them a bill or leave them a benefit?
then: That makes sense. It sounds like your children would be there for you, but the goal is really to see if we can make things easier for them instead of leaving them with one more thing to figure out.
variants: Even though they would help, would you prefer they spend that time focusing on family rather than finances?
If they had to handle it, how do you think that would affect them financially?
When you say your kids will take care of it, would that be easy for them, or would it put some pressure on them?
How would it feel knowing they could grieve and be with family instead of worrying about how to pay for everything?

instructions.text: Don't question whether the family would help — help them weigh the pressure it would create.

notes: Family: Who are you ultimately protecting with this coverage?
Family: Who would be responsible for handling everything when the time comes?
Family: What concerns you most about leaving those expenses behind?
Family: How important is it to you that your family doesn't have to worry about finances during that time?
Experience: Have you ever had to help pay for a loved one's funeral?
Experience: Have you ever seen a family struggle financially after a loss? What was that like?
Future: If something happened tomorrow, would your family know exactly what to do financially?
Future: Would they have immediate access to the funds they need? How would they handle a $10,000 to $15,000 expense?
Legacy: What kind of legacy would you like to leave behind?
Legacy: Is it important to you that everything is taken care of ahead of time?
nodes.title: Emotional discovery questions

notes: Pay close attention to: recent loss, health concerns or hospitalizations, children and grandchildren, fixed income, financial struggles, existing coverage, retirement, concerns about becoming a burden.
These are emotional openings. Rather than rushing to a quote, take time to explore them.
People rarely buy Final Expense because they want insurance. They buy because they care about the people they will leave behind.
